source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ἀγαθὸν ποιήσω ἵνα σχῶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον;

records.literal_gloss: And behold, one having come to him said, Teacher, what good shall I do that I may have life eternal?

en.L: And look, someone came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Teacher, what good [thing] must I do so that I may have eternal life?"
en.B: Then a man came up to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to gain eternal life?"
en.R: One day a man came to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?"

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, life with God that does not end
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:2 speaks of those who will rise "to everlasting life". In 19:17 the same life is called simply "life", and in 19:23-24 entering it is entering the kingdom.

decisions.choice: what good thing must I do: he thinks of a deed that will earn life
decisions.reason: He asks what single good act is needed. Jesus's answer turns him from good deeds to the one who is good.

decisions.choice: Teacher, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Good Teacher, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "Good Teacher", as in Mark 10:17 and Luke 18:18. See the note on 19:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); then (B); one day (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "one"; he is later called a young man (19:20) and rich (19:22).

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: He but said to him, Why me do you ask about the good?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Why do you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about what is good?
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Why ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about what is good?
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Why are you asking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} what is good?

decisions.choice: Why do you ask me about what is good? the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Why do you call me good? the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts of Matthew have this wording. Many later manuscripts read "Why do you call me good?", with "Good Teacher" in 19:16, as in Mark 10:17-18 and Luke 18:18-19, most likely made to agree with those Gospels. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: what is good: goodness is defined by God, not by a deed of one's choosing
alternatives: Jesus refuses to talk about goodness
decisions.reason: Jesus turns the man's question about a good deed toward God, who alone is good and who has already said what is good in his commands (Micah 6:8).

source.text: εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός· εἰ δὲ θέλεις εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, τήρησον τὰς ἐντολάς.

records.literal_gloss: One is the good; if but you want into the life to enter, keep the commandments.

en.L: One is the good [one]; but if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments."
en.B: There is one who is good. If you wish to enter into life, obey the commandments."
en.R: Only God is good. If you want to have eternal life, obey God's commands."

decisions.choice: one is good: God
decisions.reason: Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19 say "no one is good except God alone". The "one" recalls the confession that the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4).

decisions.choice: enter into life: receive eternal life (19:16)
decisions.reason: As in 18:8-9, "life" stands for the life of the age to come.

decisions.choice: One is good, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: No one is good except one, God, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts give the wording of Mark 10:18 here; see the note on 19:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Only God is good; have eternal life
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says which life is meant (19:16).

decisions.choice: which ones: which of the commands matter for this
decisions.reason: The word can mean "what sort". The man may be asking which commands count most, a question teachers debated (22:36).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who is speaking.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τὸ Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐ ψευδομαρτυρήσεις, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καὶ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus said, The You will not murder, You will not commit adultery, You will not steal, You will not bear false witness, \v 19 Honor the father and the mother, and You will love the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: And Jesus said, "'You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; \v 19 honor [your] father and mother'; and 'you shall love your neighbor as yourself.'"
en.B: Jesus said, "'Do not commit murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not give false testimony; \v 19 honor your father and your mother'; and 'love your neighbor as yourself.'"
en.R: Jesus answered, "'Do not murder anyone. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about other people. \v 19 Honor your father and mother.' And, 'Love other people as much as you love yourself.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments of the second table: Exodus 20:12-16; Deuteronomy 5:16-20
alternatives: a new list of Jesus's own
decisions.reason: Jesus names the sixth to ninth commandments and then the fifth. All of them concern how one treats other people.

decisions.choice: love your neighbor as yourself: Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: Only Matthew adds this command here. It sums up the others, and Jesus calls it the second great commandment (22:39).

decisions.choice: the: the article marks what follows as a quotation
alternatives: a word with its own meaning
decisions.reason: The Greek article introduces the list, like quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Do not commit murder; Do not commit adultery (B); Do not murder anyone (R)
decisions.reason: As at 5:21 and 5:27, Balanced and Readable give the commands in the plain form of a command.

decisions.choice: Do not tell lies about other people
decisions.reason: Readable says what false witness is.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ νεανίσκος· Πάντα ταῦτα ἐφύλαξα· τί ἔτι ὑστερῶ;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the young man, All these I have kept; what still do I lack?

en.L: The young man says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All these I have kept; what do I still lack?"
en.B: The young man said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I have obeyed every one of these. What am I still missing?"
en.R: The young man said, "I have obeyed all these commands. What else do I need to do?"

decisions.choice: young man: a man in the prime of life
decisions.reason: The word was used of men from youth to about forty. Only Matthew calls him young.

decisions.choice: what do I still lack: he senses that something is missing
alternatives: a boast that nothing is lacking
decisions.reason: He has kept the commands, yet he asks what more is needed. Jesus answers that question in 19:21.

decisions.choice: I have kept, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: I have kept from my youth, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "from my youth", as in Mark 10:20 and Luke 18:21. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε πώλησόν σου τὰ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Said to him the Jesus, If you want perfect to be, go sell of you the possessions and give to poor, and you will have treasure in heavens, and come follow me.

en.L: Jesus said to him, "If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give [them] to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Do you want to be perfect? Then go, sell your property, and give the money to people who are poor, and treasure in heaven will be yours. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Jesus told him, "If you want to be perfect, go and sell everything you own. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have riches in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, whole, lacking nothing
decisions.reason: This is the word of 5:48. It answers the man's question "what do I still lack?". Being whole means giving God undivided love, here shown by giving up wealth to follow Jesus. It does not set up a second, higher level of disciple.

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: what God keeps for those who give and obey
alternatives: a reward earned by good deeds
decisions.reason: As in 6:19-21, what is given away for God is kept by God.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: the call to be a disciple
alternatives: a request to walk with Jesus that day
decisions.reason: These are the words Jesus used to call the fishermen and Matthew (4:19; 9:9). The way to life is to follow Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: riches
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ νεανίσκος τὸν λόγον ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard but the young man the word he went away grieving, he was for having possessions many.

en.L: But when the young man heard this word, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
en.B: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he owned a great deal of property.
en.R: When the young man heard this, he was very sad, and he went away. He was very rich.

decisions.choice: grieving: sad and troubled
decisions.reason: The verb means to be sorrowful. He wants eternal life but will not let go of his wealth.

decisions.choice: possessions: property, likely land and goods
decisions.reason: The word is used of property, especially fields and estates (as in Acts 5:1).

decisions.choice: He was very rich
decisions.reason: Readable states the point simply.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πλούσιος δυσκόλως εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν·

records.literal_gloss: The and Jesus said to the disciples of him, Truly I say to you that a rich [man] with difficulty will enter into the kingdom of the heavens;

en.L: And Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Truly I tell you that a rich [{{gender:person|man}}] will enter the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty;
en.B: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Truly I tell you, a rich person will find it hard to get into the kingdom of heaven.
en.R: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "I tell you the truth, it is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: with difficulty: hardly, only with great trouble
decisions.reason: The word means hard to do. The next saying (19:24) shows how hard.

decisions.choice: a rich person: wealth holds people back from following Jesus
decisions.reason: As the young man just showed, wealth can hold a heart so firmly that a person will not give it up for God (6:24).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: a rich [{{gender:person|man}}]
decisions.reason: The saying is about any rich person.

source.text: πάλιν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρυπήματος ῥαφίδος εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Again and I say to you, easier it is a camel through eye of a needle to go than a rich [man] into the kingdom of the God.

en.L: And again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than [for] a rich [{{gender:person|man}}] [to enter] into the kingdom of God."
en.B: I say it again: a camel could pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could enter the kingdom of God."
en.R: I will say it again. It would be easier for a camel to go through the hole in a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
decisions.reason: The camel was the largest animal in the land and the eye of a needle the smallest opening. The picture is meant to be absurd, like the camel swallowed in 23:24. The disciples' question and Jesus's answer (19:25-26) show that it is impossible for people.

decisions.choice: a real camel and a real sewing needle
alternatives: a narrow gate in Jerusalem called the Needle's Eye
a rope, by a change of one letter
decisions.reason: The story of a small gate called the Needle's Eye is told only centuries later, and there is no evidence for such a gate in Jesus's day. The reading "rope" is found only in a few late manuscripts. Both try to soften a saying meant to shock.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: the same as the kingdom of heaven in 19:23
decisions.reason: Matthew usually says "kingdom of heaven" but sometimes "kingdom of God" (12:28; 21:31, 43). The two sayings stand side by side here.

decisions.choice: a rich [{{gender:person|man}}]
decisions.reason: As in 19:23.

decisions.choice: the hole in a sewing needle
decisions.reason: Readable says what the eye of a needle is.

source.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο σφόδρα λέγοντες· Τίς ἄρα δύναται σωθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: Having heard and the disciples were astonished greatly saying, Who then is able to be saved?

en.L: And when the disciples heard [this], they were greatly astonished, saying, "Who then can be saved?"
en.B: The disciples were utterly amazed at this. "Then who can be saved?" they asked.
en.R: When Jesus's followers heard this, they were very surprised. They asked, "Then who can be saved?"

decisions.choice: greatly astonished: wealth was widely seen as a sign of God's blessing
alternatives: surprised that rich people were mentioned
decisions.reason: The law promised plenty to those who obey (Deuteronomy 28:1-14). If even the rich, who seemed blessed, cannot enter, the disciples ask who can.

decisions.choice: be saved: be rescued for the life of the age to come
alternatives: be kept safe in this life
decisions.reason: In this passage being saved means having eternal life (19:16) and entering the kingdom (19:24).

decisions.choice: were astonished: the imperfect tense, they kept on being amazed
decisions.reason: The tense pictures continuing amazement.

source.text: ἐμβλέψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις τοῦτο ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν, παρὰ δὲ θεῷ πάντα δυνατά.

records.literal_gloss: Having looked at [them] and the Jesus said to them, With men this impossible is, with but God all things possible.

en.L: And Jesus looked at [them] and said to them, "With {{gender:human beings|men}} this is impossible, but with God all things [are] possible."
en.B: Jesus looked straight at them and said, "For human beings this cannot be done, but for God everything is possible."
en.R: Jesus looked at them and said, "People cannot save themselves. But God can do anything."

decisions.choice: this: being saved
alternatives: a camel going through a needle
decisions.reason: "This" refers to the disciples' question. No one, rich or poor, can bring about salvation by human power.

decisions.choice: with God all things are possible: the words to Abraham and Sarah
decisions.reason: God asked, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?" when he promised Sarah a son (Genesis 18:14). Job confesses that God can do all things (Job 42:2).

decisions.choice: looked at them: looked intently
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a steady, searching look.

decisions.choice: {{gender:human beings|men}}
decisions.reason: As in 9:8, the word means human beings.

decisions.choice: People cannot save themselves
decisions.reason: Readable says what is impossible.

source.text: Τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι· τί ἄρα ἔσται ἡμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Then answering the Peter said to him, Behold we left all things and followed you; what then will be to us?

en.L: Then Peter answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, we have left everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; what then will there be for us?"
en.B: Then Peter spoke up. "We have left everything behind and followed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}," he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "So what will we receive?"
en.R: Then Peter said to Jesus, "We left everything we had to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So what will we get?"

decisions.choice: we: emphatic, set against the young man who would not leave his wealth
decisions.reason: Peter speaks for the Twelve. They have done what the young man refused to do (4:20, 22; 9:9).

decisions.choice: what will there be for us: what reward will we have
decisions.reason: Peter asks about the treasure in heaven Jesus promised (19:21).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οἱ ἀκολουθήσαντές μοι ἐν τῇ παλιγγενεσίᾳ, ὅταν καθίσῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ, καθήσεσθε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπὶ δώδεκα θρόνους κρίνοντες τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: The and Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you that you the [ones] having followed me, in the regeneration, when sits the Son of the Man on throne of glory of him, will sit also you on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of the Israel.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you that you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, in the renewal [of all things], when the Son of Man sits on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne of glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, when all things are made new and the Son of Man takes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne, you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will also take your seats on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth, God will make the whole world new. Then the Son of Man will sit on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne as king. And you who have followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will also sit on twelve thrones. You will judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the renewal: the new birth of the world in the age to come
alternatives: the new birth of a believer
decisions.reason: The word means a rebirth. Here it is the making new of all creation that the prophets promised (Isaiah 65:17; 66:22), when the Son of Man reigns.

decisions.choice: in the renewal goes with "you will sit"
alternatives: it goes with "you who have followed me"
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between the two. It most naturally says when the disciples will sit on thrones, not when they followed Jesus.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man on his throne of glory: Daniel 7:9-14
alternatives: a throne in the present age
decisions.reason: In Daniel thrones are set up and one like a son of man receives an everlasting kingdom. Matthew speaks again of the Son of Man's throne of glory in 25:31.

decisions.choice: judging: ruling over, and passing judgment on
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures to judge Israel often means to govern it, as the judges did. It may also include judgment at the end. The twelve disciples answer to the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: God will make the whole world new
decisions.reason: Readable says what the renewal is.

decisions.choice: glorious throne
decisions.reason: "Glorious" keeps the key term in its adjective form.

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὅστις ἀφῆκεν οἰκίας ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου, ἑκατονταπλασίονα λήμψεται καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσει.

records.literal_gloss: And everyone who left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of the name of me, a hundredfold will receive and life eternal will inherit.

en.L: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit eternal life.
en.B: Anyone who has left behind houses, or brothers or sisters, or father or mother, or wife or children, or fields, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be repaid a hundred times over and will receive eternal life as an inheritance.
en.R: Some people have left their homes, their brothers or sisters, their father or mother, their wife or children, or their land, because they follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They will get back a hundred times more than they left. And God will give them eternal life.

decisions.choice: for the sake of my name: because of me, for loyalty to me
alternatives: for the sake of a title
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. Compare 10:22, "hated by all because of my name".

decisions.choice: a hundred times as much: far more than was given up, in the family of God's people
decisions.reason: Jesus calls those who do God's will his brothers, sisters and mother (12:49-50). Mark 10:30 says the reward comes "now in this time", together with eternal life in the age to come.

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as heirs, a gift and not a wage
decisions.reason: An inheritance is given because one belongs to the family. Compare 25:34.

decisions.choice: or wife and a hundred times, the readings of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no mention of a wife, in some early manuscripts
many times, in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "or wife", and some read "many times" for "a hundred times", as in Luke 18:30. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with the reward told after the list
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the long list.

decisions.choice: God will give them eternal life
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the inheritance.

source.text: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.

records.literal_gloss: Many but will be first last and last first.

en.L: But many [who are] first will be last, and [the] last first.
en.B: But many who are first now will end up last, and the last will end up first.
en.R: But many people who are important now will be the least important then. And many who are the least important now will be the most important then.

decisions.choice: first and last: those who rank high or low now will change places in the kingdom
alternatives: the order in which people enter heaven
decisions.reason: Those who seem first now, like the rich, may be last; those who seem last, like the disciples who gave everything up, will be first. The same saying ends the parable that follows (20:16).

decisions.choice: but: a warning that follows the promise
alternatives: a contrast with the young man only
decisions.reason: After promising reward, Jesus warns that rank in the kingdom will not follow the ranks of this world, even among his followers.

decisions.choice: important now ... least important then
decisions.reason: Readable says what first and last mean.

decisions.choice: no closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer to Peter goes on into the parable of 20:1-16, which begins "For the kingdom of heaven is like". The speech closes at 20:16.
